_comment: Pins are authored deliberately and never generated from a run.
A MEASUREMENT pin sits at the current number: it cannot fail on anything
that exists today, only on new dead content. That is the ratchet stopping
regrowth, and it does not by itself force work.
A TARGET pin is set where the number should be. The section is EXPECTED to
sit out of band until the work lands; that is the point of it.
A pin may carry both a limit and a target: the limit fails the build, the
target states the direction of travel. There is no third kind — the
presence of both max and target is the signal, and the shape says so.
`kind` is a note for whoever reads this file. The generator branches on the
section's DIRECTION, declared in status.py, and never on `kind`. A pin key
naming no section is refused rather than silently doing nothing.
RE-PINNING IS NOT WIDENING, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHETHER SOMEONE LOOKED.
Raising a ceiling because a section went red is widening: it converts a
failure into a pass and answers a question by not asking it. Moving a pin
after a reviewed, deliberate change is maintenance: the number moved for a
reason a person read and accepted. The test is not the size of the move, it
is whether the reason was examined before the pin followed it.
_expected_red_comment: Deliberate reds, enumerated. A red test not on this list is a regression.
ADD THE ENTRY IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT ADDS THE TEST. Otherwise the build
goes red as an unexpected regression, and the fastest-looking fix is to
revert the test — which deletes the finding it was written to hold.
Each entry names the finding it encodes and the condition that deletes it.
Two promoted findings still land here when their tests are written:
archetype spread and boss band. Hits-to-die and ability-lane parity have
arrived; each was pinned to a target the game does not meet, which is the
point of a target pin and the reason both are red on purpose.
_expected_red: Combat.Chassis.DamageBelowHealth :: Monster damage growth outruns gear defence growth by 3.76x across the levelling range (damage x13.78, defence x3.67), so hits-to-die falls from level 1 to 50 and a player at cap is one-shot by content they out-gear. DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: the O91 retune lands and the damage exponent comes down far enough that the ratio reaches 1.0. Do not close it by raising gear defence — O91 rules that direction out explicitly.

Progression.PowerBand.AbilityLane :: Ability parity measures 0.647x at the cap against O99's ruled 0.85-1.15x, and 0.388x at endgame where the section is unpinned. An ability-geared build's ability lane composes to 65% of a weapon-geared build's weapon lane at the same gear depth, and the deficit WIDENS with gear depth rather than diluting - a lane with more lines compounds harder up a back-loaded ladder. Crit and More cancel exactly; the shortfall is flat 1.000 against 1.154 and increased 3.35 against 4.49. DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: ability affix breadth is authored, the flat-half question is answered, and the cap measurement reaches the band. Do not close it by widening the band, and do not close it by letting ability hits read the weapon pool - that is the partition deleted, not the gap closed.

Progression.PowerBand.AtCap :: The at-cap band measures 6.53x against an authored 8-10x, on a baseline definition corrected 2026-08-22 (a realistically decent roll two tiers below what item level allows, derived identically at both measurement points; it was previously the theoretical worst roll, which made the number uninterpretable). DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: the owner rules on the band targets against the corrected basis — either the authored 8-10x moves, or content retunes until the measurement reaches it. Do not widen the assertion to make it pass.

silent-nodes.why: Drive this down regardless. A node a player spends a point on and gets nothing from is a broken promise, and it is the failure this project has shipped four times.

dead-tags.why: 118 of 202 looks alarming and is not all rot. Some is deliberate reserve ahead of consumers, which O72 now makes the required order: widen the vocabulary first, then author to it. The rest is the real backlog. Nobody has separated the two, and until someone does, this pin only stops the number growing.

unmapped-stat-targets.why: Lowered 7 -> 6 by wiring DashCooldown, which was never blocked on anything: the comment recording it as unwireable claimed EBreakerAggregatedAttribute had no dash entry, and it had one when that was written. Before that, lowered 8 -> 7 when the section stopped counting rider-delivered targets as unmapped: O98 rules MeleeDamage a tag-keyed slice of the weapon pool, so it will never have a lane and counting it made a ratcheting ceiling that could not reach zero. Before that, lowered 10 -> 8 by the O54 pool split, which wired WeaponDamage and AbilityDamage. They were the only entries ever blocked on something larger than a line of aggregation: there was ONE damage bucket and a partition needs two. A ceiling that does not fall after a real drop has stopped being a ratchet.

empty-lanes.why: Raised 8 -> 9 by wiring DashCooldown. Worth stating because it was predicted NOT to move, on the reasoning that gear already bids into DashCooldownReduction: this section counts NODE authors, not bidders, so a lane gear bids into still reads empty until a node reaches it. That is the section working — the tree is the layer it measures. Before that, raised 6 -> 8, and this is the one shape of increase the pin file permits: O72 orders the work as vocabulary first, then authoring, so a newly wired lane necessarily lands here for exactly as long as it takes content to reach it. WeaponDamage and AbilityDamage have lanes, gear affixes and a measured parity figure; no NODE authors them yet. If this number is still 8 after a tree pass, the pass skipped the lanes it was waiting for.

uncalled-generation.why: Already zero. Pinned so it stays that way.

unimplemented-invariants.why: Re-pinned 51 -> 48: PowerBand.AbilityLane was written by the O54 pool split, and the split added two invariants to power-and-scaling that landed WITH their tests rather than ahead of them. Pinned so it cannot grow, targeted so it does not sit there for a year. Order: the four promoted findings first; then anything guarding a newly written and therefore unenforced rule — the three-pool model, the rewrite caps, the axis-overlap prohibition, equip caps at save load; then the rest, with the systems they describe.

loot-per-hour.why: The reference figure the drop pipeline is tuned against, at the reference area level. Band rather than ceiling: too few items is as wrong as too many.

power-band-atcap.why: Measures 6.53x on the corrected baseline. Whether 8-10x was ever derived or seeded is an open question; the pin holds the authored target until it is answered.

power-band-ability.why: O99. Measures 0.647x at the cap. THE BAND CLOSES BY AUTHORING CONTENT, NOT BY TOUCHING THE COMPOSITION. The two builds hold an identical More product and identical crit lines, so both cancel exactly and parity is the flat ratio times the increased ratio - and both are short, in two different ways. INCREASED, 3.35 against 4.49: the ability pool is one seeded line per slot at placeholder values where the weapon pool is that line plus added damage, fire rate, five conditional lines and the projectile family. That half is unauthored content. FLAT, 1.000 against 1.154: the ability lane has no flat line at all, because Added Damage bids Flat into the weapon lane only and O54 names three INCREASED pools without settling the flat half. That half is an unanswered design question and is in the open list. Anyone reading this as a plumbing problem will 'fix' it by folding the weapon pool back into ability hits, which deletes the partition rather than closing the gap. Target, not measurement: 0.647x pinned would enshrine abilities as a second-class lane, the same mistake as pinning the defence inversion at 3.76.

power-band-endgame.why: Measures 15.40x, comfortably inside. Now meaningful, because both bands finally compute their baseline the same way.

damage-vs-defence-growth.why: Measures 3.76 — monster damage grows x13.78 across the levelling range while gear health grows x3.67, so hits-to-die falls the whole way. O91 rules that the damage exponent comes down until this reaches 1.0; defence does not scale up to meet it. Target, not measurement: pinning at 3.76 would enshrine the inversion.

rewrite-impact.why: Worst single rewrite step on an optimized build, 1.46x. Ceiling rather than band: a rewrite worth nothing is a design problem, not a build-breaking one.

offered-to-spendable.why: 0.63x on the worst tree. The largest gap in the report.

node-shape-composition.why: 52% is close enough that the band is the target rather than the measurement.
